rubric.why: Checks that stable equilibrium restores the body to its original position after a small displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a slightly displaced body returns to its original position.

rubric.why: Checks that the body stays in its new position in neutral equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a slightly displaced body remains in its new position.

modelAnswer: In stable equilibrium, a body returns to its original position when slightly displaced.
In neutral equilibrium, a body remains in its new position when slightly displaced.

items.followUp: State the steps of the head-to-tail rule and explain how to draw the resultant of two vectors.

rubric.why: Checks the required arrangement of the vectors.
rubric.description: Places the vectors head to tail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tail of each successive vector is placed at the head of the previous vector.

rubric.why: Checks how the resultant is drawn.
rubric.description: States the direction of the resultant vector.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

modelAnswer: Place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first vector, and continue this for any further vectors.
The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

items.followUp: Define efficiency and calculate the percentage efficiency of a system that gives 60 J of useful output from 100 J of input.

rubric.why: Checks that efficiency is defined as a ratio of useful output to input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying efficiency as useful output divided by input.

rubric.why: Checks the percentage-efficiency relationship.
rubric.description: Writes the formula for percentage efficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula: percentage efficiency = (useful output ÷ input) × 100%.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of the useful output work (or energy) to the input work (or energy) of a system.
Percentage efficiency = (useful output ÷ input) × 100%.

items.followUp: Convert 68°F into Celsius using the Fahrenheit-to-Celsius relation.

rubric.why: Checks use of the correct conversion relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using C = (5/9)(F − 32).

rubric.why: Checks the converted temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer, approximately 37.8°C.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 100°F
Formula: C = (5/9)(F − 32)
Substitution: C = (5/9)(100 − 32) = 37.8°C
Answer: 100°F = 37.8°C (approximately)

items.followUp: State the law of inertia and give two everyday examples of it.

rubric.why: Checks the law's description of motion and the condition needed to change it.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that a body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an external force.

rubric.why: Checks a correct example of inertia of motion.
rubric.description: Gives the example of a passenger moving forward when a vehicle stops.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as a passenger being thrown forward when a moving bus stops suddenly.

rubric.why: Checks a second correct example of inertia of rest.
rubric.description: Gives the example of a passenger moving backward when a vehicle starts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as a passenger being thrown backward when a bus starts suddenly.

modelAnswer: The law of inertia states that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an external force.
When a moving bus stops suddenly, passengers tend to move forward.
When a bus starts suddenly, passengers tend to move backward.

items.followUp: Find the volume of a metal object of mass 3 kg and density 7500 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the given mass and density in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying m = 5 kg and ρ = 8200 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: Checks selection of the density-volume relationship.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using V = m/ρ.

rubric.why: Checks correct substitution of the given values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting V = 5 kg ÷ 8200 kg m⁻³.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated volume and its SI unit.
rubric.description: Calculates and gives the volume in cubic metres.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct volume with unit; award 1 mark if the calculation is correct but the unit or rounding is missing.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 5 kg, ρ = 8200 kg m⁻³
Formula: V = m/ρ
Substitution: V = 5 kg ÷ 8200 kg m⁻³
Calculation: V = 0.0006098 m³
Answer: V ≈ 6.1 × 10⁻⁴ m³

items.followUp: A force of 20 N makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Find its perpendicular horizontal and vertical components.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of resolution as splitting a force into components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing resolution as splitting a force into components.

rubric.why: Checks that the components act in specified directions and together represent the original force.
rubric.description: Explains the role and orientation of the components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the components together have the same effect as the original force and identifying the angle with the horizontal.

rubric.why: Checks the horizontal component relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fx = F cos θ.

rubric.why: Checks the vertical component relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Fy = F sin θ.

modelAnswer: Resolution of forces is the process of splitting a force into components along specified directions, whose combined effect is the same as that of the original force.
For a force F making an angle θ with the horizontal, the perpendicular components are horizontal and vertical.
Horizontal component: Fx = F cos θ
Vertical component: Fy = F sin θ

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring instrument, and what is the least count of a ruler marked in millimetres?

rubric.why: Checks that least count refers to the smallest measurable quantity.
rubric.description: Identifies the least count as the smallest measurement an instrument can make.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the least count is the smallest value measurable by an instrument.

rubric.why: Checks that the value is measurable by the instrument, not merely a scale label.
rubric.description: Completes the definition of least count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the smallest measurement the instrument can measure accurately.

modelAnswer: The least count of an instrument is the smallest measurement that it can measure accurately.
